categories.name: Consume
categories.description: Watching, reading, or listening to content someone else made.

categories.name: Create
categories.description: Making, writing, drawing, designing, or building something. The primary activity is producing or editing the thing itself - the user is actively making the output.
examples: building out a website, portfolio, or profile for your own identity
using design software (e.g. Figma) to make a design
using a video editor to produce a video
exclusions: a tool used as a means to an outcome rather than the creative work itself (e.g. an image/file/unit converter, a compressor, a calculator) - that's Solve, even if it technically modifies a file

registering or signing up for a domain, account, or service - the transactional act of acquiring something is Solve, even when what you're acquiring is for your own identity or a future creative project

categories.name: Play
categories.description: Games, sports, instruments. If it is a game, it is ALWAYS Play - a slow, ambient, relaxing, cozy, or meditative game is still Play, never Relax.

categories.name: Learn
categories.description: Studying, practicing, or conducting active in-depth research on a specific subject or skill the user is trying to understand or improve.

categories.name: Explore
categories.description: Open-ended browsing, discovery, or looking something up with no specific ongoing task, project, study objective, or defined purpose.

categories.name: Connect
categories.description: Communication and relationships: the primary purpose is communicating with or maintaining relationships with other people.

categories.name: Collect
categories.description: Saving or archiving something for later reference, records, or claims. This is about preserving something for later, NOT primarily for immediate use.
examples: things that need to be retained

categories.name: Relax
categories.description: Ambient or passive experiences intended to unwind or establish a mood. The user is not trying to accomplish a task, study something, communicate, create something, or actively interact with the content.
exclusions: games (a game is ALWAYS Play, never Relax, regardless of pace or tone)

categories.name: Solve
categories.description: Tools being actively used to accomplish or move something forward. The primary activity is using a tool to accomplish a task - the tool is the means to an outcome, rather than the creative work itself.
examples: editors used as utilities (not to produce creative output)
services used to complete a task
registering a domain, account, or service
trackers and live dashboards (e.g. gas fee tracker, price tracker)
